_description: Case 3: load the L-shaped pattern case 02 produced (fixtures/l_shape_seed.val) rather than building from empty, confirm the loaded geometry via pattern.dump, then convert the L back into a plain rectangle by extending the notch out to the full square and rebuilding the piece's node list around the new corner -- exercising 'import an existing pattern and modify it', not just 'build from scratch'.
_editVsRebuildChoice: No 'edit an existing object's formula in place' action exists in this phase's action layer (documented gap -- see tests/actionlayer/README.md); the rebuild approach from the task spec is used instead: ONE new point G is added at the full-height corner (200mm up from B, bypassing the notch points C/D/E's own 140/60/60 formulas entirely, so it lands exactly where F's own 200mm height puts the opposite corner), two new lines connect it into the outline (B-G, G-F, reusing the existing A-B and F-A lines from the L-shape import), and a brand-new 'Rectangle' piece is built from nodes [A,B,G,F]. C, D, E and the four L-shape-only lines (B-C, C-D, D-E, E-F) and the original 'LShape' piece are left in the pattern file, unused by the new piece -- there is no delete/remove action in this phase to clean them up. golden_diff.py and this case's own README section check the 'Rectangle' piece's own node/line count (4/4), not the whole file's object count, for exactly this reason.
